session_game.title: Public Speaking Arena
session_game.description: Present to an AI audience. Handle Q&A, manage stage fright, and master the art of speaking with confidence.

help_content.what_is: A public speaking simulator where you present to an AI audience that reacts in real-time. Each audience member has a different personality — from supportive listeners to tough questioners. Practice presentations, handle Q&A, and build confidence.
tips: Start with a hook — a story, question, or surprising fact
Structure your talk: Introduction, 3 key points, Conclusion
Use the 'rule of three' — group ideas in threes
Pause for emphasis — silence is powerful
End with a clear call to action
Practice your opening and closing — they matter most

content_structure.description: Was the presentation well-organized with clear structure?

delivery_confidence.description: Was the delivery confident, natural, and engaging?

audience_engagement.description: Did they keep the audience interested throughout?

clarity_simplicity.description: Were complex ideas explained simply and clearly?

qa_handling.description: How well did they handle questions from the audience?

memorable_impact.description: Would the audience remember this talk?

persona_pool.name: Ishaan Patel
persona_pool.personality: Genuinely curious and eager to learn. Asks innocent but sometimes surprisingly deep questions. Represents the audience member who wants to understand your topic.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: That's interesting, but can you explain how that actually works in practice?

persona_pool.name: Prof. Raman Iyer
persona_pool.focus: challenging claims, testing knowledge depth, finding holes
persona_pool.personality: Academic and rigorous. Asks tough questions to test whether the speaker truly knows their topic. Not hostile — genuinely testing competence. Respects well-defended points.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: You cited a 2019 study, but more recent research contradicts that. How do you reconcile?

persona_pool.name: Rhea Malhotra
persona_pool.personality: Starts out uninterested. Checks phone frequently. Tests whether you can re-engage a disengaged audience. Will perk up if you tell a good story or make it relevant to her.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: Sorry, I zoned out. Can you summarize why this matters to me?

persona_pool.name: Dr. Kavita Nayak
persona_pool.personality: Warm and encouraging. Nods along, asks supportive questions. But also gives honest constructive feedback. The audience member every speaker wants.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: Great point! Can you elaborate on the practical implications of that?

persona_pool.name: Sameer Thakur
persona_pool.personality: Disruptive and attention-seeking. Makes sarcastic comments, challenges your credibility, and tries to throw you off. Tests your composure and ability to handle disruption gracefully.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: Come on, you can't seriously believe that. Do you even have experience in this field?

persona_pool.name: Anjali Krishnamurthy
persona_pool.focus: implementation, real-world application, feasibility, next steps
persona_pool.personality: Highly practical. Wants to know how to apply what you're saying. Not interested in theory alone. Asks 'so what?' and 'how do I use this?' questions.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: Interesting theory. But how would a small business actually implement this tomorrow?

persona_pool.name: Rajat Saxena
persona_pool.focus: domain knowledge, trends, competitive landscape, nuance
persona_pool.personality: Deep domain expertise. Tests whether you're surface-level or truly knowledgeable. Will call out oversimplifications but respects nuanced perspectives.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: You're oversimplifying. The reality in this industry is much more complex because...

persona_pool.name: Maya Desai
persona_pool.focus: stories, personal connection, emotional impact, authenticity
persona_pool.personality: Connects through stories and emotions. Loves speakers who share personal experiences. Gets moved by authenticity. Will call out speakers who feel robotic or scripted.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: The data is fine, but do you have a personal story that shows why this matters to you?

scenarios.title: College Presentation — Final Year Project
scenarios.description: Present your final year project to a panel of professors and classmates. You have 10 minutes to showcase months of work. Make it count.
scenarios.setting: A college auditorium. Your slides are up on the projector. 50 classmates sit in the audience, and 3 professors are in the front row with evaluation sheets.
scenarios.session_topic: Presenting a final year engineering/MBA project to academic panel
coaching_tips: Start with the problem you solved, not the technology you used

storybook_pages.title: Months of Work
storybook_pages.text: Six months of coding, testing, and debugging. Your final year project is ready. Now you have 10 minutes to present it to the panel. Everything rides on this presentation.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian engineering student preparing presentation slides late at night, laptop with project code, scattered notes, determined, digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Auditorium
storybook_pages.text: 50 classmates fill the seats. Three professors sit in front with evaluation sheets. Your slides load on the projector. The clicker feels heavy in your hand.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian college auditorium, student at podium, professors in front row with clipboards, classmates in audience, presentation slides on screen, digital art

storybook_pages.title: You're On
storybook_pages.text: The professor nods: 'You may begin.' Deep breath. Click to the first slide. Your voice fills the room. This is your moment.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian student at podium beginning presentation, first slide visible, audience attentive, college auditorium, spotlight moment, digital art

scenarios.title: TED-Style Talk — Share Your Idea
scenarios.description: Give a 5-minute talk about an idea worth spreading. No slides, just you and your words. Engage, inspire, and leave the audience thinking.
scenarios.setting: A round red carpet on a small stage. A single spotlight. 200 people in the audience. No podium, no slides — just you and a microphone.
scenarios.session_topic: Delivering a TED-style talk about an idea worth spreading
coaching_tips: Tell a personal story that connects to a bigger idea
No jargon — speak so anyone can understand

storybook_pages.title: The Red Carpet
storybook_pages.text: A round red carpet. A single spotlight. 200 faces looking at you. No slides to hide behind. No podium to grip. Just you, a microphone, and an idea worth spreading.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: TED-style stage with red circular carpet, single spotlight, Indian speaker stepping into light, audience silhouettes, inspirational atmosphere, digital art

storybook_pages.title: Your Idea
storybook_pages.text: Everyone has one big idea. Something they've learned, experienced, or discovered that could change how people think. Tonight, you share yours in 5 minutes.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian speaker with lightbulb visualization above head, inspirational pose, warm stage lighting, thought bubbles forming, digital art

storybook_pages.title: The First Word
storybook_pages.text: The host introduces you. Applause fades. Silence. 200 people wait for your first word. Make it count — the opening defines the talk.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Close-up of Indian speaker at microphone, stage lights, expectant audience in background, powerful moment of beginning, digital art

scenarios.title: Industry Conference — Keynote Address
scenarios.description: You're the keynote speaker at a major industry conference. 500 professionals expect insights, not fluff. Deliver value or lose the room.
scenarios.setting: A large conference hall. 500 industry professionals, live streaming, and press coverage. Your company's reputation is on the line.
scenarios.session_topic: Delivering a keynote address at a major industry conference
coaching_tips: Have clear takeaways the audience can act on

storybook_pages.title: The Big Stage
storybook_pages.text: 500 professionals. Live streaming to thousands more. Three journalists in the front row. Your CEO texted: 'Don't mess this up.' No pressure.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Large Indian tech conference hall, 500 attendees, massive screen behind stage, cameras recording, keynote speaker about to go on, digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Expectations
storybook_pages.text: Last year's keynote went viral — for the wrong reasons. The speaker rambled for 45 minutes with no substance. The bar is low, but the expectations are high.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Backstage at Indian conference, speaker reviewing notes, stage manager giving countdown, energy and pressure visible, digital art

storybook_pages.title: Command the Room
storybook_pages.text: The lights dim. Your name appears on the screen behind you. You walk to the center of the stage. 500 faces turn toward you. Own this room.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian professional walking onto conference stage, name displayed on massive screen, audience applauding, confident stride, spotlights, digital art

scenarios.title: Best Friend's Wedding — The Toast
scenarios.description: Your best friend is getting married and you're giving the toast. 300 guests, emotional families, and one chance to make it perfect. No pressure.
scenarios.setting: A beautifully decorated wedding reception hall. 300 guests at tables. All eyes turn to you as you stand up with the microphone.
scenarios.session_topic: Delivering a heartfelt and entertaining wedding toast
coaching_tips: Keep it under 3 minutes — shorter is better

storybook_pages.title: Your Best Friend
storybook_pages.text: You've been friends since school. Shared lunches, survived exams, celebrated first jobs together. Now they're getting married, and they asked you to give the toast.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Montage of Indian friendship memories - school days, college, first jobs, leading to wedding, warm nostalgic digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Reception
storybook_pages.text: 300 guests at beautifully decorated tables. Grandparents, cousins, college friends, office colleagues. The DJ hands you the microphone. The room goes quiet.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Beautiful Indian wedding reception, decorated hall with flowers and lights, 300 guests at tables, person standing up with microphone, digital art

storybook_pages.title: Speak from the Heart
storybook_pages.text: Your friend looks at you from the head table and smiles. Their partner squeezes their hand. This isn't about being perfect — it's about being real. Go.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian wedding toast moment, speaker holding microphone, bride and groom smiling from head table, warm golden lighting, emotional atmosphere, digital art

scenarios.title: Crisis Communication — Addressing the Team
scenarios.description: Bad news has hit your company. Layoffs, product failure, or a PR crisis. You must address 100 anxious employees and maintain morale while being honest.
scenarios.setting: A company all-hands meeting room. 100 employees sit with worried faces. Rumors have been flying for days. You're the one who has to tell the truth.
scenarios.session_topic: Addressing employees during a company crisis with honesty and empathy
coaching_tips: Be honest — people can handle truth better than uncertainty

storybook_pages.title: The Crisis
storybook_pages.text: The news dropped yesterday. Your company's biggest client pulled out. Revenue dropped 40%. The board decided on restructuring. 100 employees are about to hear news that changes their lives.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian corporate office, emergency meeting being called, worried employees checking phones, hushed conversations, tense atmosphere, digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Responsibility
storybook_pages.text: As the leader, it's your job to tell the truth. Not sugarcoat it, not dodge questions. Stand up there and be honest, while somehow keeping this team together.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian leader standing alone in empty meeting room, preparing remarks, weight of responsibility visible, corporate office at night, digital art

storybook_pages.title: Face the Team
storybook_pages.text: 100 faces look at you. Some angry, some scared, some resigned. They need honesty, clarity, and hope — in that order. You step to the front. 'I owe you the truth.'
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian corporate town hall, leader at front facing 100 anxious employees, serious but compassionate expression, crisis meeting atmosphere, digital art

transfer_exercises.game_context: Managing resources across multiple rounds to reach the best outcome
transfer_exercises.real_world: Planning study time over a semester rather than cramming before exams
transfer_exercises.challenge: Create a resource management plan for your next month: budget time/money/energy across competing priorities.

transfer_exercises.game_context: Recovering from negative events across game rounds
transfer_exercises.real_world: Maintaining performance after setbacks in a sports season or project
transfer_exercises.challenge: Track your energy/mood for 5 days. Notice patterns. What depletes you? What restores you?

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting among alternatives based on available information and values.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between two career paths based on income, passion, and long-term growth.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Good decision-making combines rational analysis with awareness of cognitive biases that distort judgment.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Leaders make high-stakes decisions daily — the quality of their process matters as much as the decision itself.

glossary_terms.definition: Analyzing information objectively to form a well-reasoned judgment.
glossary_terms.example: Questioning whether a statistic is representative before using it to make a decision.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Critical thinking involves identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, and considering alternative perspectives.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Journalists fact-check before publishing; scientists replicate experiments before claiming discoveries.

glossary_terms.definition: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning from failure.
glossary_terms.example: Seeing a poor game result as feedback on what to practice, not evidence of being bad at the game.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research by Carol Dweck shows people with growth mindsets achieve more and recover better from setbacks.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Students who believe intelligence is fixed give up when challenged; those with growth mindset persist and improve.

achievements.name: Fact Finder
achievements.description: Used strong evidence in every argument

title: Public Speaking
description: Face a virtual audience and practise the structure, delivery, and presence that make a speech memorable. From opening hook to closing call-to-action — own the room.
coaching_moment: Face a virtual audience and practise the structure, delivery, and presence that make a speech memorable. From opening hook to closing call-to-action — own the room.
cultural_context: Public speaking confidence is among the most consistently cited skill gaps in India's graduate workforce. From college campus placements to TED-style conferences, the ability to speak with clarity and conviction opens doors across India's professional landscape.
learning_objectives: Develop critical thinking through debate gameplay
Build self-awareness about your strengths and areas for growth
reflection_prompt: Which argument from the other side actually made you reconsider? Why?
